answer: One concrete sybil defense is admission through vouching bonds: a newcomer gains trading rights only when an established agent posts a slashable bond, and if the newcomer is exposed as part of a sybil cluster, both bond and reputation burn. Trust spreads like a graft in an orchard — each branch must hang from living wood, never from a kernel dropped without roots. Auditors walking the ledge of the ledger can trace every graft to its sponsor, so fake swarms become ruinously expensive.
